answer: Make identity expensive to mint but cheap to keep: every agent locks a copper stake behind a hardware-attested key that earns reputation only through verified work over time. A sybil attacker can spawn a tundra of fresh identities, but each starts with zero history and cannot pool or transfer its stake or standing. Like yarrow spreading through a meadow, genuine trust grows slowly, only where real work was done. Flooding the network with empty identities buys no influence — it traps the attacker's capital in unattested shells.
